sections.content: Daily life depended on agriculture, exchange and religious practices. The gerund (*cultivando*, practicando) describes two actions happening at the same time — useful for showing how different parts of daily life ran in parallel.

items.spanish: Muchas familias vivían cultivando la tierra y participando en rituales religiosos a la vez.
items.english: Many families lived cultivating the land and taking part in religious rituals at the same time.

items.spanish: Mientras unos intercambiaban productos mediante el trueque, otros trabajaban las tierras comunales.
items.english: While some exchanged goods through barter, others worked the communal land.

items.spanish: La religión acompañaba la vida cotidiana, marcando los ciclos agrícolas y sociales.
items.english: Religion accompanied daily life, marking the agricultural and social cycles.
Barter allowed goods to be exchanged.

sections.content: *Cultivando* / practicando / *marcando* show an action running alongside another — distinct from the imperfecto, which just describes one ongoing background action.
